Dinner with an exec/friend at a large national property management company tonight. This person oversees ~150k apartments; access to an insane amount of data. 

Current multifamily market in most of the country is worse than S&L, .com bust, or the GFC. Worst they’ve seen. 

Class A mostly fine, decent rent growth. However:
- credit scores at class A have gone down meaningfully over the past 3 years. 
- more people are paying rent via credit card. 
- average bank account balance noticeably lower than even 2 years ago
- class A tenants stretched thin, living beyond their means. 20k comes in, 20k goes out every month. 
- starting to see these renters move down a tier 

Class B:
- simply too many apartments, we built too much new stuff. Ripple effect is enormous. 
- fewer renters tomorrow than today. Same store foot traffic noticeably down year over year. Some markets down 40-50%
- considering dropping rents below $700 a month on some 1beds in major southern markets.

posts.name: The Transcript
posts.text:
$META Q3 Earnings: Interesting numbers on Muse AI

— 10M+ users signed up in just six weeks, despite availability being limited to the U.S. and Canada.
— ~25% of users engage daily, more than 2x the initial engagement of Threads.
— 25%+ of users engage in shopping, with an average purchase size exceeding $200.
— Personal productivity (email, calendar management and task automation) and creativity rank as Muse’s second and third most common use cases, respectively.
— Targets a 10x+ improvement in inference cost efficiency over the next 12 months.
— Meta is building compute capacity to serve 1B+ Muse users over the next few years.
— Muse monetization will begin earlier than Meta's traditional playbook, reflecting high inference costs and significant commerce opportunities.
— Meta expects Muse to eventually generate more revenue per U.S. user than its existing Family of Apps

posts.text:
ACTIVE ETFS MAKE UP ONLY ABOUT 11% OF THE ETF MARKET, BUT THEY'RE PULLING IN ABOUT 37% OF ALL ETF FLOWS

Fidelity's head of ETF strategists Craig Ebeling says one group is driving it

And it's not retail investors

"In the advisor space, they're really leading the charge with active ETF adoption."

On the advisor side, he said that share of flows is closer to 47% this year.

"Most financial advisors have worked with active managers in the past. They have the tools, the know-how to figure out skill versus luck."

He said there's nothing wrong with indexing, but advisors can bring clients other options if they want to go above and beyond.

"Your average retail investor can't look at 20 ETFs that are all active and maybe more expensive than the index and figure out, all right, this one's going to be better than that one."

posts.text:
CHARLIE MUNGER EXPLAINED HOW THE US WENT FROM HORRIBLE RECESSIONS TO A CENTURY OF EXTREME PROSPERITY

Then he warned about the one question no economist can answer

"In the old days, when people thought the currency should be backed with gold, and they wanted the inflation rate to be zero and the social safety net to be almost zero, they created a lot of GDP growth and a lot of prosperity, but with horrible recessions. And to some extent, the recessions automatically cured themselves.

When we got into the business of big interventions, driven by the example of the Great Depression, what we got is pretty much a century of extreme prosperity with relatively minor recessions.

But we're using methods that are so extreme that maybe we can't use a lot more of them. And we don't know the answer to that.

If an economist told me he knew the answer to that, I wouldn't believe him either way. It wouldn't matter which way his opinion was. I just think we don't know."

BREAKING: Dutch spies hacked Jared Kushner's iPhone and watched him access a Dubai bank account holding hundreds of millions funneled from Azerbaijan, part of at least $2 billion MBS and MBZ placed for him after he promised to push their agenda with Trump, per a Vanity Fair excerpt.

"Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy. He promised MBZ that he'd push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off," a source who knew the arrangement said.

The money was meant to redraw the region's map and lock in normalization with Israel. Roughly $1 billion of it was deposited in Israel's Central Bank for Kushner, with Netanyahu requiring dual-key approval on any transfers.

The two royals initially discussed more than $10 billion for a shared slush fund. That narrowed to roughly $2 billion deposited into accounts Kushner could access, including roughly $750 million at First Abu Dhabi Bank under a UAE charity us

posts.text:
BREAKING: Global equity funds are now on track to attract +$1.3 trillion of inflows in 2026, the largest annual intake on record.

This would exceed the previous annual record set in 2021 by ~35%.

At the same time, US equity funds are on pace to post record inflows of +$636 billion, or nearly 50% of the total.

This means investors have allocated +$511 billion to these funds year-to-date.

Global technology funds are on track to attract a record +$196 billion in 2026.

This would be more than double the +$75 billion recorded in 2025.

Global investor appetite for equities has never been stronger.
